newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Asia leads Israeli export growth in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Asia leads Israeli export growth in 1996.

text.p: Israeli merchandise exports to Asia grew about 20 percent in the first 11 months of the year from the same time in 1995 and accounted for half of total export growth, the Israel Export Institute said on Sunday.

Exports to the United States rose just 2.2 percent and those to the European Union by 5.9 percent in the period. All told, Israeli merchandise exports, not counting diamonds, rose 7.6 percent in the first 11 months to $12.8 billion.

The institute's chairman, Amir Makov, said in a statement that while this was down from 10.7 percent growth in 1995, the figure pointed to the export sector's underlying strength in the face of monetary policy that has hurt export profitability.

Makov said the especially slow export growth to the United States was due to the freezing of the shekel-dollar exchange rate. This hurt export profitability to the U.S. market and was forcing exporters to direct sales elsewhere.
He added that high technology exports were growing quickly. Electronic components was the fastest-growing export sector, rising 18.4 percent in the 11 months, the institute said.
